title: Field-level confidence before reducing human review of generated docs
situation: The team has a custom documentation skill / slash command that updates README sections, API references, and migration notes after refactors. The command's overall acceptance rate is high, but review data shows that incorrect outputs are concentrated in a few fields, especially function signatures and migration warnings.
question: What should the team do before reducing human review?

options.A: Approve documentation changes when the command's file-level confidence exceeds a fixed threshold.
options.B: Require field-level confidence outputs and calibrate review thresholds using labeled validation examples.
options.C: Switch the command to plan mode for all documentation updates before applying changes.
options.D: Use aggregate acceptance rate as the release gate and sample merged outputs weekly.

why: For reliability-sensitive generated documentation, a useful unit of review is often the field, not the whole file. A README update may be mostly correct while still containing a wrong function signature or an unsafe migration note, so a single aggregate metric can create a false sense of readiness. The stronger pattern is to have Claude output field-level confidence alongside the generated values and compare those confidence scores against a labeled validation set. Calibration turns confidence from a model self-report into an operational routing signal, for example sending low-confidence function signatures and ambiguous migration warnings to human review while allowing well-calibrated low-risk fields to proceed. This is a human-review workflow design problem, not just a prompting-mode problem. Claude Code features such as planning, skills, and repository context help with development workflows, but they do not replace segmented validation and calibrated thresholds. (Docs: Claude Code overview, define success criteria.)
concrete_task: claude -p "update the README section..." --json-schema '{fields:[{name,value,confidence}]}' then route low-confidence fields to review.

tasks.prompt: Update the README API reference for formatDate after its null fix (read src/utils/formatDate.js and README.md). Return fields: 'signature', 'behaviour_on_null', 'migration_warning', 'example'. Give each a value and your calibrated confidence (0-1) that the value is exactly correct for this codebase.

expected_outcome: The documentation update returns one confidence per field. The runner routes fields under 0.8 (and every signature or migration warning under 0.95) to human review instead of trusting a file-level score.

rubric.criterion: every field carries a confidence in [0,1]
the signature field is present for calibration against labelled examples
learner explains why a file-level threshold or aggregate acceptance rate hides field errors
